title: ci: stage-aware lint adapters and background dependency-heatmap sweeper
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Split monolithic lint runner into stage-aware adapters to reduce presubmit latency; add a lightweight background job (dep-heatmap-sweeper) to surface and prune stale dev dependencies. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Summary: Implement stage-aware lint adapters to enable fast 'quick' lint lanes and heavier 'full' lanes, and add a background dependency-heatmap sweeper that periodically computes dependency usage hotspots and emits pruning suggestions for devdeps. Motivation: the monolithic lint runner has long lead times for small changes and forces opt-in for dependency hygiene. This change reduces presubmit feedback for small edits while operationalizing dep surface reduction across the org.

What changed (high level): commits: - f3d9b2c: add stage-aware lint adapter framework (Go) - 7a1c8d1: split existing linters into quick/full adapters and wire them into presubmit manifest - b2c3e4f: add dep-heatmap-sweeper service and ingestion pipeline - c1d2e3a: add small cron job + k8s job spec for sweeper - e5f6g7h: update release hooks to tolerate short quiet windows during sweeper rollouts

Design notes: - Stage-aware adapters: adapters are lightweight wrappers (Go) that map a presubmit profile to a set of linters and a time budget. Quick adapter runs a small subset and returns diagnostics; full adapter runs the complete suite. Adapters are pluggable and load their policy from a new presubmit-profiles YAML file. - Dep-heatmap-sweeper: periodically scans CI job artifacts and dependency resolution traces to build a key-value heatmap of devdependency usage frequency across repos. A scoring heuristic flags low-usage devdeps for human review and optionally suggests package.json/pyproject cleanup PRs. The sweeper emits metrics and a small summary JSON to an S3-compatible bucket. - Rollout: staged rollout behind a feature-flag. Default for initial rollout: quick adapter on all PRs, full adapter on pushes to release branches and nightly runs. Sweeper runs once per 24h in staging and once per week in prod during the initial month.

Files touched (representative): - ci/presubmit/adapters/go/adapter_main.go - ci/presubmit/profiles/presubmit-profiles.yml - tools/sweeper/heatmap/collector.go - tools/sweeper/cron/cronjob.yaml - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (hooked to stage mapping) - infra/k8s/ci-jobs/sweeper-job.yaml

Small diff snippets (illustrative): - adapter_main.go: added stage dispatch and timeout enforcement (context with deadline) - presubmit-profiles.yml: new schema: profiles: { quick: { linters: [eslint,go vet], timeout_s: 40 }, full: { linters: [eslint,go vet,staticcheck,python-flake], timeout_s: 900 } } - collector.go: top-level scan loop and s3 upload util added

Testing and CI: - Unit tests added for adapter dispatch and profile parsing. - Integration test for sweeper ingestion (local-mode) that runs against a small artifact bundle. - Presubmit pipeline updated to run quick adapters for PRs and full adapters for nightly and release branch PRs. - CI matrix: go-tests, linter, sweeper-unit, integration-smoke. Initial CI run: one flaky integration failure in sweeper ingestion on first run (timing), re-run passed. Final CI status: all checks green.

Review conversation (high-level): - Ethan Park: "Nice separation — can we make timeout overrideable by repo via presubmit-profiles?" — Author: "Yes, profile schema supports repo-scoped overrides; added docs and example in presubmit-profiles.yml" - Ravi Singh: "Sweeper safety: don't auto-prune; ensure suggestions land as draft PRs and run tests." — Author: "Agree — current implementation only emits suggested edits as draft PRs behind a toggle; we added an explicit opt-in annotation to enable auto-cleanup per-repo." - Lina Martinez: "Concern about extra load on artifact storage when scanning historical traces." — Author: "Added incremental windowing (7 days by default) and a shard key to bound I/O; also added a staging warm-up before expanding retention window." - QA (Amira K.): "Flaky test noted, resolved by increasing test artifact generation timeout; added to flaky-tests.md"

Backward compatibility and safety: - No changes to external API. - New components are feature-flag gated. - Sweeper runs in read-only mode by default and only opens draft PRs when explicitly enabled.

Operational impact: - Introduces a small Go binary (adapter) and a lightweight sweeper service. - Resource estimate: adapters negligible (run inside existing presubmit workers), sweeper modest: 0.5 vCPU + 1GB RAM for initial staging; configurable. - Observability: added metrics: presubmit.adapter.duration{profile}, sweeper.heatmap.shards_processed, sweeper.suggested_cleanups_count. Dashboards added under CI/Presubmit.

Migration and rollout plan: - Phase 1 (week 0): enable quick adapter as default for all PRs in a canary org and run sweeper in staging daily. - Phase 2 (week 2): expand quick adapter org-wide, add nightly full runs for critical repos. - Phase 3 (week 4): enable suggestion PRs to repo maintainers (drafts). - Rollback: flip feature flag or revert workflow change; adapters are nonblocking and fall back to legacy runner if misconfigured.

Merge notes: squashed and merged via squash merge after approvals (Ethan, Ravi) and green CI. See merge commit fef2a3b.

Follow-ups: - ENG-2341: add automatic heuristic tuning for heatmap thresholds - ENG-2350: publish developer docs and migration quickstart - CHORE: add small runbook for sweeper failures

References: Linear ENG-2248 (presubmit latency), SUP-413 (customer report on noisy devdeps).
